title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator
platform: International Space Station (ISS), Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME
summary: Gaseous fuels (C2H4 and CH4 diluted with N2) burned on 25 mm and 50 mm porous circular burners in the CIR aboard the ISS under quiescent microgravity to emulate condensed-phase fuel burning and determine extinction limits across varying O2 concentrations.

tests.notes: Test day 2019-Feb-8 (CSV row 1). Porous circular burner 25 mm. Flames ignited that day: 10 (count not split by O2 level). The table lists approximate O2 levels of tests that ignited; this level is one of them. Outcome set to no_sustained_burn: the PSI-20 research impacts say flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time. Chamber pressure is not given per test; assumed 14.7 psia (101.3 kPa), the pressure PSI-20 investigation page, Objective 1 pairs with 21% O2 among the NASA atmospheres to be examined. Source note: Oxygen Conc. (as diluted with nitrogen on a volume basis) was varied between tests where approximate concentrations for tests that ignited are listed. The chamber pressures were also varied but are not identified in this summary table.
